extracted.intended_audience: home cooks / domestic cooks (historical, general readership)
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and practical rules for preparing puddings, cakes, breads, and related baked/fried dishes (19th-century domestic cookery). Emphasis on technique, ingredient preparation, and heat/handling requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid poaching eggs when mixing with hot milk
rubrics_metrics.description: When they are to be mixed with milk, let it cool after boiling, or the eggs will poach; and only set it on the fire a few minutes, to take off the raw taste of the eggs, stirring it all the time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cool boiled milk before adding beaten eggs; if reheating, do so only briefly while stirring to remove raw egg taste and avoid curdling/poaching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wash and thoroughly dry currants
rubrics_metrics.description: Currants require washing in many waters to cleanse them; they must be picked and well dried, or they will stick together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rinse repeatedly and dry completely to prevent clumping in mixtures and uneven distribution in doughs/puddings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blanch and treat almonds to prevent oiling
rubrics_metrics.description: Almonds should be put in hot water till the skins will slip off, which is called blanching; they must always be pounded with rose or orange flower water, to prevent their oiling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Blanch to remove skins and pound with flavored water (rose/orange) so they do not release oil that could affect texture/flavor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add cream at the last moment and avoid over-beating
rubrics_metrics.description: When cream is used, put it in just before the mixture is ready; much beating will decompose it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fold or add cream only at the final stage to preserve its structure; avoid excessive mechanical agitation that breaks down cream.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have all ingredients prepared before beginning
rubrics_metrics.description: Before a pudding or cake is begun, every ingredient necessary for it must be ready; when the process is retarded by neglecting to have them prepared, the article is injured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mise en place—measure, wash, peel, slice, and have pastry/paste ready so the process proceeds promptly and quality is maintained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure oven and vessels are in proper state
rubrics_metrics.description: The oven must be in a proper state, and the paste in the dishes or moulds, ready for such things as require it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preheat and manage oven temperature and ensure moulds/dishes are ready to receive batters or pastes to avoid under- or over-cooking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promptness in handling and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Promptitude is necessary in all our actions, but never more so than when engaged in making cakes and puddings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work quickly and with appropriate sequencing; delays during mixing/assembly can adversely affect rise, texture, and final quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Always beat eggs light before use
rubrics_metrics.description: When only one or two eggs are to be used, cooks generally think it needless to beat them--it is an error: eggs injure every thing, unless they are made light before they are used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whip eggs (or whites/yolks as specified) to recommended froth/lightness to incorporate air and avoid dense/heavy results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use proper cloth for boiling puddings
rubrics_metrics.description: Cloths for boiling puddings should be made of German sheeting; an article less thick, will admit the water, and injure the pudding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose dense, appropriate boiling cloths (German sheeting) to keep water out and protect pudding texture during boiling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Puff paste technique and handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Sift a quart of flour... make up the remainder with cold water into a stiff paste... wash the salt from a pound of butter, divide it into four parts, put one of them on the paste in little bits, fold it up, and continue to roll it till the butter is well mixed... touch it very lightly with the hands in making--bake it in a moderate oven, that will permit it to rise, but will not make it brown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate butter in stages, handle paste lightly to preserve layers, and bake in a moderate oven to allow lift without undue browning. Good paste should look white and as light as a feather.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove salt from butter before using in pastries
rubrics_metrics.description: Wash the salt from a pound of butter... (repeated in multiple recipes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rinse salted butter when recipes call for 'washed' butter to reduce saltiness that could adversely affect pastry taste and texture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seasoning and small-batch addition improves flavor
rubrics_metrics.description: To each quart of [mincemeat] add a tea-spoonful of pounded black pepper, and one of salt; this greatly improves the flavour, and can be better mixed with a small portion than with the whole mass.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When seasoning large batches, season samples or small portions first to control final flavor uniformly before combining with full batch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify and cool jellies carefully; remove grease and dross
rubrics_metrics.description: When the feet are boiled... strain the liquor... when cold, take all the grease off... whip up the whites to a froth, crush the shells and put with them, mix it with the jelly... stir it occasionally till the jelly is melted, but do not touch it afterwards. When it has boiled till it looks quite clear on one side, and the dross accumulates on the other, take off carefully the thickest part of the dross, and pour the jelly in the bag; put back what runs through, until it becomes quite transparent--then set a pitcher under the bag, and put a cover all over to keep out the dust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remove fat from cooled stock, use egg whites (and crushed shells) to clarify, avoid excessive stirring after initial melt, skimming dross carefully, and filter through cloth; protect from dust while setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use appropriate bag/frame for straining jellies
rubrics_metrics.description: The bag should be made of cotton or linen, and be suspended in a frame made for the purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspend a cotton/linen bag in a frame to filter jellies; reuse what passes until clear and keep covered to avoid contamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Colour and ingredient selection influences jelly appearance
rubrics_metrics.description: The feet of hogs make the palest coloured jelly; those of sheep are a beautiful amber-colour, when prepared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select animal source according to desired jelly coloration and flavor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tie boiled/steamed puddings appropriately (tight vs loose)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sweetmeat pudding... tie it in a cloth securely... when done, pour melted butter... Plum pudding... tie it loosely, that the pudding may have room to rise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust tightness of boiling cloth depending on the recipe: some puddings require tight tying to keep shape, others must be tied loosely to allow expansion and rising.

rubrics_metrics.name: Raisins/currants: dust with flour to prevent sinking or sticking
rubrics_metrics.description: Raisins for puddings or cakes, should be rubbed in a little flour, to prevent their settling to the bottom--see that it does not stick to them in lumps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coat dried fruit lightly with flour to keep them suspended in batter; avoid clumping by separating pieces before incorporation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage oven temperature to suit the item (moderate/quick/slack)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bake in a moderate oven... bake quickly in a quick oven... bake in a slack oven (for gingerbread).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match heat level to recipe: moderate for puff paste and many puddings, quick for drop biscuits and certain cakes, slack/low for dense gingerbreads; adjust baking time accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beat to lightness (eggs/sugar/flour/other) to ensure proper texture
rubrics_metrics.description: Beat eight eggs very light, add to them a pound of flour sifted, and a pound of powdered sugar; when it looks quite light... Pound cake: 'work the butter to a cream... put alternately into the butter, sugar, flour, and the froth from the eggs... continuing to beat them together till all the ingredients are in, and the cake quite light.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In many cakes and puddings, success depends on thorough beating to incorporate air—follow specified order of folding/alternation for best lift and lightness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect custards from water during setting
rubrics_metrics.description: Pour in a quart of rich boiled custard--set it in water, and make it boil till the custard is set--take care the water does not get into it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using bain-marie/water-bath, prevent water ingress into custard or delicate fillings by guarding rim and proper dish placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: For fried items, fry quickly to light brown and drain well
rubrics_metrics.description: Fry them quickly of a light brown, drain them well, put them in a dish, sprinkling sugar over each, and glaze them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use hot fat to ensure quick frying to a light brown; drain excess fat after frying and finish with sugar/glaze as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid discolouration for delicate cookies (macaroons, biscuits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Be careful not to let them get discoloured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch baking closely for delicate items that must remain pale; remove promptly from oven to avoid browning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use appropriate consistency for batters/doughs (smooth, not lumpy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Make it sufficiently thick with corn meal and a little salt; it must be mixed perfectly smooth--stir it constantly till done enough. When making bread... taking great care that it be smooth, and quite free from lumps; beat it some minutes...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure batters and doughs are smooth and lump-free before cooking; constant stirring and proper mixing techniques prevent uneven texture or scorching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Store flour in a closed chest/box for best preservation
rubrics_metrics.description: When you find the barrel of flour a good one, empty it into a chest or box, made for the purpose, with a lid that will shut close: it keeps much better in this manner than when packed in a barrel, and even improves by lying lightly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep flour in a well-sealed container to protect from moisture and pests and to maintain quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bread dough proportions and early handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Put into a bowl two gills and a half of water for each quart, with a tea-spoon heaped up with salt, and a large spoonful of yeast for each quart; stir this mixture well... pour a little of the mixture on to wet it, then more, until you get it all in... take one-third of the flour out of the kettle, pour on the batter, and sprinkle over it the dry flour; stop the kettle, and set it where it can have a moderate degree of warmth: when it has risen well, turn it into a bowl, mix in the dry flour, and knead it on a board till it looks quite light.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow specified water:flour:yeast proportions, build batters/doughs in stages, keep at moderate warmth for fermentation, and knead until light/elastic for good bread structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finish and handling of bread dough before baking
rubrics_metrics.description: In the morning, take the dry crust carefully from the top, put the dough on a board, knead it well, make it into rolls, set them on tin sheets, put a towel over, and let them stand near the fire till the oven is ready.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After first rise, degas/reshape, form rolls or loaves, cover and allow final proof in a warm place before baking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rasp bread when baked
rubrics_metrics.description: The bread must be rasped when baked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform specified finishing (rasping) on the crumb/crust of bread immediately after baking as a customary finishing step (historical instruction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Make and preserve patent/pressed yeast carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: Put half a pound of fresh hops into a gallon of water, and boil it away to two quarts... make it a thin batter with flour; add half a pint good yeast, and when well fermented, pour it in a bowl, and work in as much corn meal as will make it the consistency of biscuit dough; set it to rise, and when quite light, make it into little cakes, which must be dried in the shade, turning them very frequently; keep them securely from damp and dust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concentrate hop tea, ferment with yeast, combine with corn meal to form cakes and dry gently in shade; store dry and protected from damp/dust to preserve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate simple yeast maintenance methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons who live in town, and can procure brewer's yeast, will save trouble by using it: take one quart of it, add a quart of water, and proceed as before directed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substitute brewer's yeast suitably diluted for homemade patent yeast when available to save labor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rehydrate and prepare dried yeast cakes before use
rubrics_metrics.description: Take one or more cakes, according to the flour you are to make; pour on a little warm water; when it is dissolved, stir it well, thicken with a little flour, and set it near the fire, to rise before it is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reconstitute dried yeast cakes in warm water, feed with flour to build a sponge, and proof in a warm place before incorporation into dough.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative potato-based yeast starter
rubrics_metrics.description: Peel one large Irish potato, boil it till soft, rub it through a sieve; add an equal quantity of flour, make it sufficiently liquid with hop tea; and when a little warmer than new milk, add a gill of good yeast; stir it well, and keep it closely covered in a small pitcher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use potato and hop tea as a starchy medium for a yeast starter where desired; keep starter warm and covered for fermentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare fruit/fillings and slices thin for layered desserts
rubrics_metrics.description: Put two oranges and two lemons, into five quarts of water--boil them till the rinds are quite tender; take them out, and when cold, slice them thin... lay the fruit in carefully, in alternate layers--pour on the syrup...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cook and slice fruit thinly and layer carefully with syrups/pastes for uniform texture and presentation in layered puddings/tarts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use appropriate greasing and mould preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Butter the mould, put in part of the cake, strew over it some raisins and citron--do this until all is in: set it in a well heated oven...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grease moulds and layer components as directed to prevent sticking and ensure even baking and release.
